p: hireling: Has not a hired servant some rest and ease? Then in this my continual torment I am worse than a hireling.
months of vanity: My sorrow has continued from month to month, and I have looked for hope in vain.
clothed with worms and clods of: This signifies that his disease was rare and most horrible.
a weaver's shuttle: Thus he speaks in respect for the brevity of man's life, which passes without hope of returning: in consideration of which he desires God to have compassion on him.
As the cloud is consumed and: If you behold me in your anger I will not be able to stand in your presence.
come up no more: Shall no more enjoy this mortal life.
refrain my mouth: Seeing I can by no other means comfort myself I will declare my grief in words, and thus he speaks as one overcome with grief of mind.
or a whale: Am I not a poor wretch? Why do you need to lay so much pain on me?
with dreams: So that I can have no rest, night or day.
chooseth strangling: He speaks as one overcome with sorrow, and not of judgment, or of the examination of his faith.
let me alone: Seeing my term of life is so short, let me have some rest and ease.
shouldest magnify him: Seeing that man of himself is so vile, why do you give him that honour to contend against him? Job uses all kinds of persuasion with God, that he might stay his hand.
sinned: After all temptations faith steps forth and leads Job to repentance: yet it was not in such perfection that he could bridle himself from reasoning with God, because he still tried his faith.
not be: That is, I will be dead.
